correctness.rationale: For a uniformly labelled idempotent map f:[n]->[n], k roots yield exactly binom(n,k)k^(n-k) maps and the labelled species exp(z exp(z)). Choosing ordered disjoint (s+1)-element stars yields the exact factorial-moment identity (n)_(j(s+1)) I_(n-j(s+1))/(s!)^j. The adjacent k-weight ratio is strictly decreasing; log ratio expansion near r+2log r=log n+1 places k at n/r with n/K_n=r+o_P(1). Conditional multinomial allocation of n-k leaves among k roots gives mean ~r^(s+1)/s! and vanishing relative variance for fixed s; the explicit second factorial moment validates the concentration. The displayed ratio and log-concavity control the tails by a decaying geometric series (n/r^3 -> infinity), not merely a local saddle heuristic. A q-round component-matching Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse argument for each fixed q proves completeness of the limit theory; finite subsets of star-multiplicity axioms hold w.h.p., implying the FO zero-one law by compactness. Finite model property follows from finite unions of required stars; infinitely many finite star-size 1-types preclude omega-categoricity. Boundaries n>=1, s fixed, no uniform s(n) claim. Proof is coherent on all quantifiers and boundaries.

originality.rationale: Harris-Schoenfeld already count labelled idempotent transformations, and Sachkov analyzes the number of fixed points: neither accessible statement gives the fixed-s small-component asymptotic, specified limit theory, and non-omega-categoricity as a combined classification. Koponen Example 2.2 provides deterministic bounded-parent height-one structures and FMP background, not this uniform labelled random limit. Compton's component-method literature may imply the logical zero-one consequence abstractly, but this does not by itself supply the exact (log n)^(s+1)/s! normalization. Claiming independently novel species enumeration or the general EF technique would be inappropriate; novelty is the model-specific combined sharp small-star law and logical classification, subject to the inaccessible historic primary literature.

value.rationale: The natural random idempotent map class has a sharp vector of logarithmic-size star multiplicities and an explicitly identified first-order almost-sure theory. The constants 1/s! and non-omega-categoricity distinguish it from mere total enumeration or a formal textbook example; this provides asymptotic counts of genuinely definable finite components plus a complete logical classification.

limitations: The proof does not give uniformity for s growing with n nor a rate of FO convergence.
Direct enumeration through n=6 is finite corroboration, not a proof of n->infinity.
